name: Califone
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: What was left of Red Red Meat went through the junk drawer of American music and came back with bottles, hand drums, tape hiss and a heron-headed god from Tim Rutili's dreams.

eras.title: Red Red Meat, and what it cost
eras.text: Before Califone there was Red Red Meat, Rutili's Chicago blues-rock band on Sub Pop. It toured with the Smashing Pumpkins, lost its bassist Glynis Johnson to AIDS, and got stranger with every record. By 1997 it had run its course, and most of its people followed Rutili into the next thing.

years.h: Friends of Betty renames itself Red Red Meat
years.p: Rutili's Chicago band, which had included Ben Massarella, becomes [[Red Red Meat|d2952878-d32a-4e09-b6c8-6f9598e5cfbe]] once Glenn Girard joins. Glynis Johnson, his partner since film school, plays bass.

years.h: The engineer from Idful takes the drum stool
years.p: Red Red Meat cuts its first single, Hot Nikkety Trunk Monkey, at Idful Studios with [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]]. Idful co-founder [[Brian Deck|e91d5dc5-12a7-45cf-af2b-f120def0f711]] ends up as the full-time drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Red Meat · Wikipedia: Tim Rutili
years.h: Glynis Johnson dies of AIDS-related complications
years.p: Johnson leaves Red Red Meat after its summer 1992 tour with the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]]. According to Wikipedia she dies that fall; she and Rutili had been together for years.

years.cap: Red Red Meat on stage, Rutili at the mic
years.h: Jimmywine Majestic brings the second drummer back
years.p: Massarella returns on percussion beside Deck's kit on Red Red Meat's Sub Pop album. The two-drummer clatter turns into a Califone trademark.

years.h: The last Red Red Meat album, then Rutili alone at home
years.p: There's a Star Above the Manger Tonight closes the Sub Pop run. The band effectively stops, and Rutili starts recording by himself.

eras.title: Little pop songs out of found pieces
eras.text: Califone began as a home project, with Red Red Meat's blues still in it and everything else up for grabs: old folk, electronics, Psychic TV, silent movies. Friends from Chicago drifted in until it was a band.

q: Now it seems like just about anything goes.
years.h: Rutili starts Califone as a home project
years.p: The plan was little pop songs made out of found pieces, a bedroom experiment with no band attached.
years.xp:
Rutili described it later as "supposed to be just a little home project, and it slowly grew from there." Tape loops and junk-shop instruments got stitched into songs, and players from Red Red Meat and other Chicago bands rotated in over time.

The name comes from Califone International, the audio equipment maker whose sturdy record players filled American classrooms.

years.h: The first Califone release is an EP on Flydaddy
years.p: Rutili makes Califone with Red Red Meat's Tim Hurley, and Flydaddy Records puts it out.

years.h: Roomsound is the first full album, on Perishable
years.p: Chicago's Perishable Records releases it. Dead Oceans reissues it with extras in 2016.

years.h: Rutili, Massarella and Deck join Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock
years.p: As [[Ugly Casanova|5c2d7596-2366-47c5-b4a2-0550ac8f9e69]], the three and [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]] of [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]] make Sharpen Your Teeth for Sub Pop, with Deck producing and drumming.

years.h: Silent movies get a live Califone score
years.p: The band had been playing live soundtracks to silent-era films, and Deceleration One collects the instrumental results. Deceleration Two followed in 2003; parts three and four were talked about and never came out.

eras.title: The heron king arrives on Thrill Jockey
eras.text: Califone made the three records that defined it for Thrill Jockey. Songs started as improvised jams and got their words, loops and junk percussion later. The Chicago Tribune and the New York Times took notice, and the band spent long stretches on the road in Europe and the US.

years.h: Califone moves to Thrill Jockey with Quicksand/Cradlesnakes
years.p: It's the first of three albums on the Chicago label.

years.cap: Tim Rutili and Ben Massarella on stage in Chicago
years.h: A recurring bird dream becomes Heron King Blues
years.p: The band improvised the basic tracks in three days at a studio on Chicago's South Side. The 15-minute title track is named for a Druid god Rutili kept seeing in his sleep.
years.xp:
Rutili had dreamed all his life of a giant man-bird, and had a real fear of birds. He later matched the figure to the heron king of Druid lore, an effigy that, the legend goes, sent British soldiers running when it was raised.

Nothing was written in advance. With [[Captain Beefheart|a1594afa-2f6b-4596-a156-a35853dca691]]'s Mirror Man as the model, Massarella and Joe Adamik on percussion and Jim Becker on everything else jammed until the grooves held, then added words, steel guitar, bottles, hand drums and loops. Trick Bird was co-written with members of Orso.

years.h: Chicago Tribune picks Heron King Blues as the year's best local indie album
years.p: The paper's year-end verdict on Califone's record is that no other Chicago indie album topped it in 2004.

years.cap: Jim Becker and Joe Adamik with Califone
years.h: Califone becomes Freakwater's band on Thinking of You
years.p: Another Thrill Jockey record, with the whole of Califone behind [[Freakwater|50e68a47-b6e4-4178-84d5-8955206a0b7f]].

years.h: Califone ends up in Stranger than Fiction
years.p: The band contributes to the 2006 film's soundtrack, and starts staging animation-and-live-music pieces with filmmaker Brent Green.

years.h: Roots & Crowns gets an 8.7 from Pitchfork
years.p: Recorded between October 2005 and May 2006, it includes The Orchids, a [[Psychic TV|14c5a3a3-f5ed-4978-99af-486010e3a007]] cover. Pitchfork later puts it at No. 168 on its list of the 2000s' best albums.
years.xp: It came out as thrill 163 on Thrill Jockey. By Wikipedia's account of the reviews, the New York Times called it "enthralling."

eras.title: A ghost story with a band attached
eras.text: Rutili turned Califone into a film project: an album and a feature with the same name, which went to Sundance and then on tour with the band playing its soundtrack live. The band moved to Dead Oceans, and Red Red Meat played one last time.

years.h: Califone is the band on Flecton's The Bright Side of Dying
years.p: Ottawa's Flecton puts out the eight-song vinyl on Kelp Records with Rutili, Massarella, Joe Adamik and Jim Becker playing. It includes a [[Merle Haggard|deb2448c-6fdf-4d31-921e-757630515dbd]] cover.

years.src: Pitchfork: Califone Sign to Dead Oceans (2009)
years.h: Califone leaves Thrill Jockey for Dead Oceans
years.p: Pitchfork reports the move on July 7, 2009.

years.src: Owl and Bear: Red Red Meat to play final show (2009)
years.h: Red Red Meat plays its last show at Millennium Park
years.p: The band, reunited for a handful of shows in 2008 and 2009, plays what's billed as its final one in Chicago.

years.cap: Tim Rutili at the Rock & Roll Hotel, Washington, DC, October 25, 2009
years.h: All My Friends Are Funeral Singers is a record and a film score
years.p: Califone's first Dead Oceans album doubles as the soundtrack to a feature Rutili wrote and directed.
play: All My Friends Are Funeral Singers

years.h: Rutili's ghost film gets into Sundance
years.p: A psychic woman lives alone in the woods with ghosts she has to set free. Rutili wrote and directed, and Califone toured playing the soundtrack live under the screen.
years.xp:
Rutili described the premise simply: the woman has to find a way to release the spirits that are wrecking her life. The film starred Angela Bettis, his wife.

Instead of a normal album tour, Califone took the movie on the road and played the record as its live score.

years.h: IndiePix puts a feature film about Califone on the road
years.p: Solan Jensen and Joshua Marie Wilkinson's Made a Machine by Describing the Landscape follows the band through European and US tours after Heron King Blues.

years.h: Califone players show up on Iron & Wine's Kiss Each Other Clean
years.p: Brian Deck had produced earlier Iron & Wine records, and now members of Califone play on [[Iron & Wine|c3f28da8-662d-4f09-bdc7-3084bf685930]]'s album.

eras.title: Every song its own planet
eras.text: After a quiet spell, Tim Rutili came back writing more personally, recording away from Chicago and working with different players on every song. Califone kept going on small labels, house-concert tours and film scores, with Ben Massarella and Rachel Blumberg still at Rutili's side.

years.h: Rutili leaves Chicago and records Stitches in three states
years.p: Southern California, Arizona and Texas, with each song treated as its own planet and different musicians on each.
years.xp: Dead Oceans' notes describe garage-sale drum machines, slack guitar strings and hushed vocals next to brass, pedal steel, strings and tablas. Rutili said he forced himself to write as much as possible and to let himself be crabby and vulnerable.

years.h: Funeral Singers lands in Watch Dogs
years.p: Ubisoft puts the Califone song on the game's soundtrack.

years.h: Jealous Butcher releases Guitars Tuned to Air Conditioners
years.p: The Portland label's first Califone record follows the Insect Courage EP in March and Dead Oceans' Roomsound reissue.

years.h: Califone plays living rooms
years.p: Rutili, Massarella and percussionist Rachel Blumberg, a former [[The Decemberists|97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3]] drummer, tour house concerts and small rooms as a trio.

years.h: Echo Mine follows on Jealous Butcher
years.p: Four years after Guitars Tuned to Air Conditioners, it's on the same Portland label.

years.h: Villagers arrives, and a companion record follows two years later
years.p: Another Jealous Butcher release, with The Villager's Companion to come in 2025.

years.cap: Rutili and Max Knouse at the Optimal Record Store, Munich
years.h: The Villager's Companion comes out on Valentine's Day
years.p: Nine songs, opening with Every Amnesia Movie and closing with Crazy as a Loon.
